q: Existing chillers operate at 0.75 kW/ton. New units offer 0.45 kW/ton. The building runs 2,000 cooling hours/year at 500 tons peak load. What are approximate annual energy savings?
options: The savings are too small to calculate without a full energy audit
Approximately 300,000 kWh/year — improving LEED energy performance
New chillers always consume more energy during startup
The savings are exactly 50% because the new COP is 50% better
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the EA concept and solve this concept question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: energy performance: the measured or modeled energy use of a building or system; energy and atmosphere: strategies addressing energy demand, efficiency, refrigerants, and renewable energy; energy efficiency: delivery of the required service with less energy use
keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: Approximately 300,000 kWh/year — improving LEED energy performance.
logic: (0.75 − 0.45) = 0.30 kW/ton × 500 tons × 2,000 hours = 300,000 kWh/year. At $0.12/kWh = $36,000/year. This calculation type appears on the LEED exam and demonstrates why efficiency upgrades have strong financial and performance cases.

q: A project achieves 75% spatial Daylight Autonomy (sDA). What does this mean for occupants, and does it qualify for the LEED Daylight credit?
options: sDA is only measured once per year on the summer solstice
75% sDA means the building has 75 windows, which earns the credit
75% sDA is below LEED's minimum threshold of 90%
75% of regularly occupied area gets 300 lux for 50%+ of hours — qualifies for higher Daylight credit
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the EQ concept and solve this concept question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: daylight: natural light admitted into an interior space; credit: an optional LEED requirement that can earn points; minimum: the lowest acceptable value or level
keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: 75% of regularly occupied area gets 300 lux for 50%+ of hours — qualifies for higher Daylight credit.
logic: sDA uses annual climate data and detailed simulation to predict actual daylight availability throughout the year. 75% sDA means 75% of regularly occupied floor area receives at least 300 lux of daylight for at least 50% of occupied hours annually. This typically qualifies for the higher LEED Daylight credit tier (often requiring 55–75% sDA).

q: Enhanced commissioning reveals the BAS is scheduling HVAC to run 24/7 rather than following the occupied/unoccupied schedule. How significant is this?

q: During construction, workers dump concrete washout water near the site boundary where it flows into a storm drain. What LEED issue does this create?

logic: Concrete washout water (pH 11–12) is toxic to aquatic ecosystems. q: Open office occupants complain the space is too noisy for focused work. The building has high HVAC background noise. What is the fundamental LEED acoustic design issue?

Tenants should use noise-canceling headphones

logic: HVAC background noise must be in the appropriate NC range: too quiet means every conversation is audible; too loud means HVAC itself is the distraction. Office spaces target NC 35–40.
